messages:
liam: onboarding pegasus-80k int3 experimental quant. quick prefill -> at ~72k tokens we see reproducible semantic drift vs fp32 baseline. kv indices seem ok but outputs diverge. anyone seen int3 quirky RoPE interactions?

maria: int3? that's new path. which quant pipeline and runtime? can you paste repro command + a tiny diff of logits?

liam: runtime v0.22.0-intpreview, quant int3-fast. repro: ```
./longbench --model pegasus-80k-int3 --prefill 73000 --seed 2026 --dump-logits logits.int3 --baseline logits.fp32
```
Diff summary: ```
mean-l1=0.0032, max-abs=0.47 at token_idx=72345
semantic-anchor mismatch at prompt chunk starting token 72298 -> repeats different next-word choices
```

sam: interesting that kv index looks stable. can you share kv dump around that window? maybe a subtle RoPE fractional-scale displacement causes phase misalignment in attention weights.

liam: kv span dump (positions): `72000..72031`, `72032..72063`, ... `72336..72367`. nothing duplicated. but when I compare attention peak positions between int3 and fp32, there's a shift of 0.5 token in peak center for several heads.

maria: 0.5 token shift smells like a pos_scale fractional rounding when positional multiplier quantized to small integer representation. int3 compactness may be causing step quantization of the rotary multiplier. do we quantize pos multipliers?

liam: yes, int3 pipeline packs pos multipliers into a tiny LUT per-shard. resolution is ~1/256. fractional bias visible when rotary_scale != 1.0.

sam: proposal: add a microtest that compares attention position of a single head over long prefill for fp32 vs int3 and asserts peak-center delta < 0.25 tokens. if fails, we can fall back to storing pos multipliers in 8-bit for long-prefill flows.

yara: question: what's perf impact of 8-bit pos multipliers vs int3 LUT? should be small for memory but maybe affect vectorized kernels. we can measure on dedi.

liam: ran quick perf: switching pos-mul to 8-bit increased memory by ~0.18GB and reduced p50 by ~3% on long-prefill runs. accuracy restored to baseline.

maria: OK short-term mitigation: auto-upgrade pos-mul encoding to 8-bit if prefill > 60k or model.sequence_length > 60k. long-term: improve LUT interpolation (linear interpolate between nearest int3 entries) to remove 0.5-token bias.

sam: I can prototype linear interpolation in kernel to keep int3 storage but get higher effective resolution. will add a deterministic rounding mode for interpolation.

liam: created ticket ML-1508: "pegasus-80k int3: rotary multiplier quantization causes 0.5-token attention shift on long-prefill" with repro, kv-dumps, and perf numbers.

bench-bot: scheduled canary: pegasus80k-pos8-fallback -> pool:dedi-longctx-3 (24h), pegasus80k-int3-interp -> pool:dedi-longctx-3 (24h). results -> /bench/pegasus80k/int3_rope_ab. ETA 20h. :rocket:

maria: add longctx-eval goldset that checks downstream semantic pass/fail for long instructions (we see repeat/skip failure modes). also gate prod rollout until canary passes.

liam: will push microtest + ticket notes. thanks. TL;DR: int3 LUT for pos multipliers induced fractional RoPE bias causing attention peak shift ~0.5 tokens after ~72k prefill; mitigation: 8-bit fallback or interpolation; ticket ML-1508 + canary scheduled.
